decisions.rationale: Reproduced on a fresh git archive of 89161df6 with the private completed work plus one added rule per run, full public suite. An endless pulse that starts at its identity value passed all 12 tests in 5 of 5 runs on both tags with the individual scale property, 4 of 5 with a transform pulse, 4 of 5 with an endless rotation spin, and 5 of 5 as an individual-scale pulse on the gear checklist. The loop-5 test file from ea630d09 failed task 11 on every one of those pages (3 of 3 each), and an endless pulse that does not start at identity still fails 5 of 5 at 89161df6, which confirms the mechanism: the loop-6 identity helper is applied to endless animations read at or near their first frame. This is a loop-6 regression, nondeterministic, and lets a page that README task 11 forbids pass, so it is accepted. The critic's point that the checklist's pinned inline styles are never restored between the two window sizes is correct but dates from loop 3 (3d48ec9a) and is not needed to close this finding: with the fix below the checklist pulse failed 4 of 4 runs in the first window alone. Smallest correct fix: in both the checklist check and the tag check, accept identity values only when every animation on that element has finished after the finite ones are finished, and use the loop-5 strict comparison (no transform-type property other than none, zoom exactly one) while any animation on that element is still running. I verified this on a work-dir copy of the test: the four endless identity-start pulses and the spin above failed task 11 in 4 of 4 runs each with the right message, while the unmodified completed work, static identity values on all five properties, a filled fade-up entrance on the tags, a filled scale-in on the checklist and an endless opacity-only animation on the tags all passed 12 of 12 (2 or 3 runs each). Known trade-off, stated in prose: a tag that combines an endless opacity-only animation with a static identity value of a transform-type property, or with a finished identity-ending entrance, falls back to the strict check and fails task 11 (3 of 3 each under the fix, 2 of 2 passing at 89161df6); that is fail-safe, is exactly how loop 5 treated such pages, and the message names the cause. Scope: inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope, because it narrows the identity acceptance to held end values of finished animations, which is what the owner approved, with no keyframe classifier and no new mechanism.

Verified on the 89161df6 bytes. The lab.json notes still say the test rejects the transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom properties, while static identity values on all five now pass 12 of 12 (3 of 3 runs); the notes' statement that finite animations are finished first is not scoped to the checklist and the two tags, which is what the code does; and the solved-run record calls short filled entrance animations and learner transitions on the checklist and tag sizes valid variants, while README task 11 Outcome now asks that no animation or transition change the size, position or scale of the checklist or the tags. The README is the stricter, learner-facing text, so the impact is limited to maintainers and evidence readers, as the critic grades it. The task 5 sub-claim about a combined transform and zoom entrance on the checklist was not reproduced with one variant I built (it passed 12 of 12 in 3 of 3 runs); that does not change the decision, and any such failure would be fail-safe on a page the README forbids. Smallest correct fix: reword the lab.json notes to say the test rejects non-identity values of those five properties, accepts identity values only as held end values of finished animations (matching the cl6-edu-001 fix), and finishes finite animations on the checklist and the two tags only; and in the next solved-run record describe the entrance and transition variants as accepted by the test although README task 11 asks for a static layout, not as valid. Scope: inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope; it is a wording correction of maintainer and evidence text with no behaviour change.

The finding is correct and has two halves. The loop-6 half, endless transform-type animations that start at identity passing because they are read near their first frame, is the same defect as cl6-edu-001, reproduced the same way, and is closed by the fix accepted there (identity values only on elements whose animations have all finished, the loop-5 strict comparison otherwise); I verified that narrower fix, which is the critic's own narrower recommendation, on a work-dir copy of the test. Nothing in that half waits on the owner. The older half is not closed by any pre-authorized edit: an undelayed endless alternating padding animation on the overnight tag passed all 12 in 3 of 4 runs at 89161df6 and 4 of 4 at ea630d09, so it predates loop 6 and the outcome depends on the instant of reading. Closing it needs either the critic's primary recommendation, seeking each endless animation to fixed offsets inside its first iteration and reading at each, which is a new measuring mechanism beyond the approved minimal option, or widening the documented residual in lab.json and the solved-run record beyond the owner-accepted list of paused, delayed, very long or slow animations to include short undelayed endless animations, which is the owner's decision. README line 17 and task 11 Outcome already cover this case in general terms, so a learner who follows the README is not misled. Escalated for that remaining half only: the owner should choose between accepting short undelayed endless animations as part of the documented residual (then the lab.json and record wording names them and the record's endless scale variant is described as one that does not start at identity) or approving the seek mechanism. Scope: the remaining half would expand the contract either way.

Reproduced at 89161df6 with the private completed work: a static full-turn rotation written with the individual rotate property, in degrees or in turns, fails task 11 in 2 of 2 runs each with the scaling, rotating, moving or zooming message, while the same full-turn rotation written as a transform function passes 12 of 12 in 2 of 2 runs, because the transform value is checked through its matrix and the rotate value through the literal angle. Both draw the tag exactly as without them, and both are identity values in the sense the owner approved in loop 6, so the inconsistency is a gap in the loop-6 identity rule rather than a contract question. It is low, fail-safe and unlikely, and it is not a loop-6 regression, since loop 5 rejected these pages too. Smallest correct fix: decide identity for the rotate property from the rotation it describes, by building the rotation from its axis and angle and applying the same identity test already used for transform (or treating a zero axis or a whole number of full turns as identity); a matrix tolerance for floating-point residue is optional and not required. Scope: inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope, because it only completes the approved identity end value rule for one property and adds no mechanism; it changes the same file as the cl6-edu-001 fix and should land in the same correction.

Verified on the 89161df6 bytes: the lab.json notes sentence saying the test rejects the transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom properties is false since loop 6, because static identity values of all five passed 12 of 12 in 3 of 3 runs, and the earlier clause that it rejects scaling or zooming the checklist itself omits rotating and translating, which the code checks and README line 17 and the checklist message both name. This overlaps cl6-edu-002 point 1 and is maintainer-facing, so the impact is small. Smallest correct fix: in one edit of the lab.json notes, say the test rejects non-identity values of those five properties on the tags and on the checklist itself and accepts identity values only as held end values of finished animations, and correct the endless-animation sentence to match the cl6-edu-001 fix and whatever the owner decides on cl6-sme-001. Scope: inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope; wording only.
